raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"The two buffers have the same initial pH, because the source states that a 1.0 M acetic acid and 1.0 M sodium acetate solution and a 0.10 M and 0.10 M solution of the same pair have the same pH even though their buffer capacities differ [ev_001]. The 1.0 M buffer has greater buffer capacity, because it contains more acetic acid and acetate ion than the 0.10 M buffer [ev_001]. Buffer capacity is the amount of acid or base that can be added to a given volume of buffer before the pH changes significantly, usually by one unit, and it depends on the amounts of the weak acid and its conjugate base in the mixture [ev_003]. So the 0.10 M buffer has less capacity for the same reason: it contains less of each component [ev_001] [ev_003]. When a small amount of strong acid is added, the acetic acid ionization equilibrium shifts left, producing additional weak conjugate acid (acetic acid) [ev_008]. When a small amount of strong base is added, it neutralizes hydronium ion, so the equilibrium shifts right and generates additional weak conjugate base (acetate ion) [ev_008]. In both cases the added strong acid or base is converted into the weak pair members, which ionize only slightly, so the pH changes much less than it would in an unbuffered solution [ev_008]. Buffering does not mean that either solution keeps its pH unchanged for arbitrarily large additions. A buffer's action is compromised when enough strong acid or base is added to substantially lower the concentration of either member of the buffer pair [ev_003]. A buffer solution is generally no longer useful when one component is less than about 10% of the other [ev_001]. The 1.0 M buffer can absorb more added acid or base before this happens than the 0.10 M buffer, because it contains more of each component [ev_001] [ev_003].","short_answer":null,"citations":["ev_001","ev_003","ev_008"],"refusal_reason":null,"follow_up_questions":[],"confidence":0.8,"tutor_question":null,"learner_attempt_evaluation":null}
